overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique Shorts reveals that speculative cosmic survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme planetary anomalies consistently outperform all other formats, generating channel highs between 700 to 1,050+ views and 2.5% to 3.7% like rates. Conversely, short psychology trivia and duplicate re-uploads consistently stall below 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-person hazard immersion ('What If You Fell Into [Extreme Cosmic Body]?')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) led engagement and viewer velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Adopt second-person sensory immersion hooks framed around lethal, mind-bending cosmic hazards with 19–21 second runtimes.

winning_patterns.pattern: Lethal/Bizarre planetary physics with stark sensory contrasts
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme tactile physics ('Burning Ice' at 1,057 views, 'Darker Than Coal' at 1,031 views, 'Supersonic Rubies' at 725 views) dominate top percentiles.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight sensory juxtapositions (e.g., solid vs. melting, hyper-dense vs. magnetic) in the opening 2 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos covering memory or mind tricks ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' at 5–53 views across multiple iterations, 'Your Brain Is Hiding This' at 38 views, 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' at 17–71 views) repeatedly flopped.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychology facts unless framed through high-stakes survival or dark psychological micro-drama.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' decayed in impressions down to 34–118 views without viewer retention gains.
weak_patterns.action: Never re-upload the same entity; pivot to novel astronomical and scientific phenomena.
